title: U.S. Department of State — Uganda health data systems under the America First Global Health Strategy MOU, 2025
description:
"2.5.3 Funding Plan: The U.S. Government intends to provide the following amount of funding for data systems in each of the specified years, subject to the availability of funds: 2026 $26,129,831; 2027 $24,779,640; 2028 $25,103,354; 2029 $27,294,065; 2030 $9,795,399. TOTAL $113,102,289."

Uganda controls what the money builds: it "plans to determine and approve the national data and health information architecture prior to any investment financed under this MOU", the US "plans to fund data systems investments within the budget reflected in Section 2.5.3 on projects as determined jointly by both Participants", and "All data generated through U.S.-funded programs is expected to be owned by the Government of Uganda" (2.5.2).

The sum is one line of a wider MOU whose total planned US support is US$1,719,960,000 against Uganda's US$577,001,796 (Appendix 1). Non-binding: "This MOU is not an international agreement" (6.9), every figure "subject to the availability of funds".
recipient_organisation: Government of Uganda / Ministry of Health

title: Project to Enhance Distance Education Environment at Makerere University
description: KOICA grant ($12.2M, 2025) to Makerere University to transform open, distance and e-learning capabilities. Develops e-content for 2,560 courses across 10 colleges. Strengthens digital learning, research, and academic support systems.

financier: Belgian Investment Company for Developing Countries
title: TowerCo Of Africa Uganda \u2014 Rural Telecom Tower Expansion Loan
description: USD 12M 10-year senior loan to TowerCo of Africa Uganda (previously Ubuntu Towers Uganda) for installation of 506 solar-powered telecom towers in rural Uganda. Part of USD 40M syndication with EIB (USD 16M) and OeEB (USD 12M). Towers provide 4G/5G broadband coverage, mobile money access, and digital financial services to rural communities currently without mobile network coverage.

title: Scaling Agriculture Investment in Digital, AI and Innovation (SAIDAI)
description: Supports and scales digital agriculture innovations with the most potential for transformative impact, while generating evidence. Catalyses investment at scale in agricultural innovations expanding productivity, incomes and climate resilience. Drives more sustainable and better-integrated agri-food systems delivering safe and nutritious food. Builds a stronger enabling environment including better information on investment opportunities and risks. Increases deployment and adoption of technologies — including digital and AI — for greatest impact on livelihoods and resilience.
recipient_organisation: Acumen; Shell Foundation; Climate Policy Initiative; Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation

title: UGANDA TELECOM TOWER EXPANSION (TOWERCO OF AFRICA)
description: Construction of 659 new mobile sites (506 ultimately signed) in Uganda. At least 50% of towers in rural areas without mobile service coverage. Provides mobile coverage in areas without mobile broadband and increases capacity in saturated areas. Towers powered primarily by renewable energy. Enables 4G and 5G data services and mobile money solutions.

title: National Data Transmission Backbone Infrastructure/E-Government Infrastructure Phase V
description: China Eximbank government concessional loan for Phase V of Uganda's National Data Transmission Backbone Infrastructure / E-Government Infrastructure project (NBI/EGI), implemented by NITA-Uganda. Phase V extends the fibre backbone to the districts and sub-counties the first four phases did not reach and adds last-mile connectivity to government sites: 3,604 km of backbone with 51 backbone sites, 2,240 km of last mile to 800 government sites, and a new data centre at Namanve of 180 cabinets. Contractor CITCC, on commercial contract NITA-U/SUPLS/21-22/0001 signed 22 April 2022. Terms are 20 years at 2% interest (State Minister for Finance, 2023-12-06). Builds on Phases I-III (2006-2013), financed by China Eximbank, and Phase IV (2018), financed by the World Bank at US$75.8m.

title: Airtel Mobile Money Uganda \u2013 Digital Financial Services Guarantee
description: MIGA political risk guarantee covering The Rise Fund II Aurora S.à r.l. (TPG private equity) equity investment in Airtel Mobile Commerce B.V.'s subsidiary providing Airtel Money digital financial services in Uganda. Services include mobile wallet (cash-in/cash-out), airtime recharging, bill payments, merchant payments; with international transfers, savings and microloans in some markets. Risks: war and civil disturbance, expropriation, transfer restriction and inconvertibility for up to 5 years.

title: Partech Africa pre-Series B equity investment in Tugende (2022)
description: Partech Africa led a $10M pre-Series B equity round in Tugende, a Uganda-based technology-enabled MSME asset finance company operating in Uganda and Kenya. The round included participation from two new investors. Tugende uses technology to provide productive asset loans (motorcycles, smartphones) to low-income entrepreneurs and MSMEs in East Africa.

title: Uganda Digital Acceleration Project - GovNet
description: Expands Uganda's digital economy through a national government network (GovNet), digital public services, broadband connectivity, and digital inclusion.

description: D4GW-UGA (Digital for Girls and Women) Uganda component. Promotes inclusive, rights-based digital transformation across Belgium, Burkina Faso, and Uganda. Uganda component improves digital skills and digital rights for women and girls. Budget EUR 2.25M, 2021-2025. Enabel implements with Belgian government financing.

description: ITU technical assistance to Uganda for developing and implementing a National ICT Development Strategy. Activities include strategy formulation; institutional capacity building for NITA-U and Ministry of ICT; training workshops on digital economy regulatory frameworks; and support for digital transformation roadmap. Implemented January 2021 to December 2023.

title: Partech Africa equity investment in Tugende (2021 Series A extension)
description: Partech Africa and Enza Capital provided $3.6M in fresh equity to Tugende, a Uganda-based technology-enabled asset finance company that provides productive asset loans (motorcycle taxis, smartphones) to MSMEs in East Africa. The round, led by Partech, was agreed and structured in 2020 and extends Tugende's Series A. Brings total Series A equity to $9.9M.

title: Young Africa Works in Uganda
description: MCF $200M commitment to enable 4.3 million young Ugandans to access dignified work by 2030. Digital economy is a core enabling sector alongside agriculture, tourism and construction. Includes digital skills, digital platforms, and fintech access.

title: Connect Rural Uganda - Digital Inclusion (UNCDF)
description: UNCDF Connect Rural Uganda programme 2019-2026, promoting digital connectivity and financial inclusion in rural Uganda. Components include mobile broadband infrastructure, digital financial services, mobile money adoption and digital agricultural information services. Sectors covered: ICT, agriculture and education.

title: Chinese Government provides RMB 200 million grant for Customs Modernization Project in Uganda
description: On June 28, 2017, the Chinese Ministry of Commerce signed a grant agreement with the Government of Uganda worth RMB 200 million for the Customs Modernization Project. The grant agreement was signed in the Chinese capital by Matia Kasaija, Minister of Finance, Planning, and Economic Development and Dr. Qian Keming, Vice Minister of Commerce of the People's Republic of China. The grant will support the capacity of Uganda Revenue Authority (URA) to acquire latest technologies in the form of non-intrusive scanners, modernized customs risk management, supervision and communication systems, customs service and enforcement support, and border infrastructure among others. All of these advancements are intended to allow Uganda to increase the revenue collected by their Customs Agency.

title: China Eximbank provides RMB 96.9 million government concessional loan for Phase 3 of National Transmission Backbone and e-Government Infrastructure Project (Linked to Project ID#53401 and Project ID#53402)
description: On March 31, 2015, the Chinese Government and the Government of Uganda signed a preferential loan framework agreement for Phase 3 of the National Transmission Backbone and e-Government Infrastructure Project. On the same day, China Eximbank and the Government of Uganda (represented by the Ministry of Finance, Planning, and Economic Development) signed an RMB 96,966,600 ($15,391,522) government concessional loan (GCL) agreement [CHINA EXIMBANK GCL NO. (2015) 4 TOTAL NO. (543)] for Phase 3 of the National Transmission Backbone and e-Government Infrastructure Project. The Government of Uganda’s Ministry of Finance, Planning, and Economic Development then on-lent the proceeds of the GCL to National Information Technology Authority Uganda (NITA-U). The borrowing terms of the GCL were as follows: a 20 year maturity, a 5 year grace period, a 2% interest rate, a 0% default (penalty) interest rate, a 0.25% commitment fee, and a 0.25% management fee. The GCL is secured by (collateralized against) a minimum cash balance in a lender-controlled bank account (see staff comment #6 for more details). The proceeds of the GCL were to be used by the borrower to finance a $15,391,522 commercial (turnkey) contract [ID#0008000610060C] between the Government of Uganda’s Ministry of Information and Communication Technology and Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd., which was signed on July 15, 2010 and amended on December 30, 2013.   According to the Government of Uganda’s Aid Management Platform (AMP), this loan achieved a 94.8% disbursement rate, with China Eximbank making x loan disbursements (worth $14,604,878.74) between 2015 and 2017: a $4,619,644.65 disbursement on September 30, 2015, a $5,192,303.56 disbursement on September 30, 2016, a $2,145,289.98 disbursement on April 19, 2017, a $2,553,844.51 disbursement on June 28, 2017, and a $93,796.05 disbursement on December 21, 2017.
